title: Superheavy dark-bright soliton as a signature of spatial symmetry breaking transition in harmonically trapped Bose mixtures
authors: Zheng Gao, Ling-Zheng Meng, Jie Liu, Li-Chen Zhao
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of a dark-bright soliton in harmonically trapped two-component Bose-Einstein condensates and reveal an interesting spontaneous spatial symmetry breaking driven by nonlinear interactions. When the interaction parameter crosses a threshold value, we find that the dark-bright soliton's motion demonstrates a transition from symmetric periodic oscillation about the origin to asymmetric oscillations offset from the origin. In particular, at the transition point, the effective soliton mass, determined by the ratio of inertial mass to physical mass, diverges. The underlying mechanism is uncovered by constructing trial wave functions and employing the Lagrangian variational method to obtain an effective potential in the quasiparticle picture, which changes from a single well to a double well. The anomalous ``superheavy soliton'' phenomenon is a direct consequence of the dark-bright soliton's physical mass vanishing at the transition point. We obtain the phase diagram of this spatial symmetry-breaking transition. Possible implications of our finding for quantum metrology are discussed.
summary: The paper analyzes dark-bright solitons in trapped Bose mixtures, revealing that increasing interaction strength drives the system through a first-order phase transition. This transition causes the soliton's motion to spontaneously break spatial symmetry, characterized by an effective potential changing from a single well to a double well and the appearance of a 'superheavy' state.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics of dark-bright solitons in harmonically trapped two-component Bose mixtures, focusing on a spontaneous spatial symmetry breaking transition driven by nonlinear interactions.
main_result: A critical interaction parameter causes the soliton's motion to undergo a phase transition from symmetric oscillation to asymmetric oscillation, marked by the divergence of an effective mass and the formation of a double-well potential.
method: The analysis employs the mean-field approximation, deriving classical kinetic equations for the soliton using a Lagrangian variational method applied to coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations.
model_or_system: The system is a two-component Bose mixture (e.g., $^{133}	ext{Cs}$ and $^{87}	ext{Rb}$) confined in a quasi-one-dimensional harmonic trap, modeled by coupled GP equations.
key_observables: Soliton center position ($\langle X_c angle$), effective soliton mass ($M_i/M_p$), and the shape of the effective potential (single well vs. double well).
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($g_d, g_{ij}$), harmonic trap frequency ($\omega$), and the critical interaction threshold ($g_d = 1.755$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mean-field approximation and assumes weak external traps ($\omega \ll 1$) allowing for Thomas-Fermi background density approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the dynamics showing $\langle X_c angle$ and $M_i/M_p$ vs. interaction strength, highlighting divergence at the critical threshold; Figure 2 shows the dynamical phase diagram in parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the coupled GP equations, deriving an effective Lagrangian via a variational ansatz, obtaining generalized equations of motion for the soliton's center position, and analyzing the resulting potential energy landscape across different interaction regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how nonlinear interactions can induce macroscopic symmetry breaking in quantum matter waves, linking fundamental many-body physics to observable dynamical signatures like mass divergence.
